questions.stem: Arrange the following sentences into a coherent paragraph. (P) Yet the city's residents continued to complain of potholes, clogged drains and unreliable buses. (Q) Mumbai's municipal budget in 2024 was larger than the entire state budget of seven smaller states combined. (R) The gap between expenditure and delivery thus became the most telling symptom of an urban-governance crisis. (S) Clearly, money alone was not translating into civic outcomes. Correct order:
questions.explanation: Q is the opening statistic. P introduces 'Yet' — setting contrast with Q. S draws the inference ('money alone was not translating'). R states the conclusion ('thus became the most telling symptom'). Argument: Fact → Counter-observation → Inference → Conclusion.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange the sentences. (P) By the time the second monsoon arrived, the engineers were confident the dam could absorb a one-in-fifty-year flood. (Q) The first test came in July 2023, when an unexpected three-day cloudburst swelled the reservoir to 80 % capacity in 48 hours. (R) The dam was commissioned in late 2022 with much fanfare. (S) To everyone's relief, the spillway operated exactly as modelled and the water receded within a week.
questions.explanation: R introduces the dam (commissioning). Q introduces 'first test' (chronologically follows). S describes the outcome of that first test. P closes with what happened 'by the time the second monsoon arrived'. Time-marker chain: 2022 commissioning → July 2023 first test → relief → next monsoon.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) This, not any single battle, is what finally broke the empire's grip on the countryside. (Q) The colonial state had long relied on a small cadre of British officers commanding Indian troops. (R) By 1946 those very troops, having tasted Axis prison camps, returned with a changed sense of loyalty. (S) Mutinies in the Royal Indian Navy and among army personnel followed within months.
questions.explanation: Q is the setup (how the empire kept order). R introduces the break point (1946 returning troops). S shows the immediate consequence (mutinies). P delivers the verdict that this — not any single battle — was the decisive factor. Argumentative climax ordering.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) But as treatment costs climbed, so did accusations that the plan was excluding exactly those for whom it was designed. (Q) Ayushman Bharat, launched in 2018, promised free hospital care up to ₹5 lakh for the bottom 40 % of Indian households. (R) Policy-makers responded in 2024 with a doubled cap of ₹10 lakh and the addition of day-care procedures. (S) Within its first three years, millions had availed of surgeries their families could never have afforded.
questions.explanation: Q introduces the scheme. S notes immediate success. P flips to criticism ('But'). R closes with the policy response. Structure: Scheme → early success → criticism → reform response.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) The mobile phone reached rural India not through a national campaign but through sheer market pull. (Q) Operators, led by private companies, competed aggressively on call-rate per-minute, driving the cost of voice calls to the world's lowest. (R) When a farmer in a Bihar village could reach his buyer in Kolkata for less than a rupee, the phone stopped being a luxury. (S) Between 2005 and 2015 India added nearly a billion subscribers — a scale unmatched in the history of any technology.
questions.explanation: P is the topic sentence. Q explains HOW (price war). R is the concrete illustration. S gives the scale — the consequence. Standard 'topic → mechanism → example → consequence' structure.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Arrange the following sentences into a coherent paragraph. (P) After graduating, she joined a software firm in Bengaluru. (Q) Priya excelled in both academics and extracurricular activities throughout school. (R) Within a decade she had risen to become a product director. (S) Her first assignment was demanding, but she adapted quickly. Correct order:
questions.explanation: Q sets up the subject (school excellence). P follows with 'After graduating' — a temporal bridge. S shows the early-career challenge. R concludes with the long-term outcome. Pattern: Background → Entry → Early phase → Peak.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) This led to frequent power outages in several districts. (Q) The monsoon that year was far below normal. (R) Farmers were forced to rely on expensive diesel pumps for irrigation. (S) Reservoir levels dropped to historic lows. Correct order:
questions.explanation: Q is the root cause (poor monsoon). S is the direct physical effect (low reservoirs). P links reservoir shortfall to power outages. R gives the on-the-ground farmer consequence. Pattern: Cause → Physical effect → Systemic effect → Human cost.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) It allows individuals to borrow money, invest, and build financial security. (Q) Financial inclusion refers to the availability of banking services to all segments of society. (R) In India, Jan Dhan Yojana has been the flagship initiative toward this goal. (S) Without access to formal financial systems, the poor remain trapped in debt cycles. Correct order:
questions.explanation: Q defines the concept. P elaborates its benefits. S presents the cost of exclusion (contrast builds urgency). R gives the Indian example (conclusion). Definitional paragraphs typically flow: Define → Benefits → Problem without it → Solution.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) Napoleon was finally exiled to Saint Helena after Waterloo. (Q) His campaigns had reshaped the map of Europe. (R) Napoleon Bonaparte rose to power during the chaos of the French Revolution. (S) At his peak, he controlled most of continental Europe. Correct order:
questions.explanation: R is the chronological start (rise to power). Q states what his campaigns achieved. S describes his peak dominance. P is the end of the story (exile). Watch out for R-S-Q-P: S ('at his peak') logically follows the campaigns (Q), not precedes them.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) The government then launched a massive awareness campaign. (Q) Open defecation was identified as the primary cause of water contamination in rural areas. (R) Within three years, thousands of villages declared themselves open-defecation free. (S) Communities were encouraged to build and use household toilets. Correct order:
questions.explanation: Q identifies the problem. P describes the government response. S is the specific community-level action triggered by that campaign. R gives the measurable outcome. Q-S-P-R tempts because 'communities' could follow the problem, but P (government campaign) logically precedes S (community action it triggered).
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) These deposits eventually hardened into the coal seams we mine today. (Q) Vast forests covered much of the Earth during the Carboniferous Period. (R) Over millions of years, the layers were buried under accumulating sediment. (S) When these trees died, they piled up in swampy ground. Correct order:
questions.explanation: Q sets the geological scene (Carboniferous forests). S follows: 'these trees' refers back to Q's forests (pronoun lock). R explains burial (over millions of years). P gives the geological end-product. Q-R-S-P fails because R ('the layers') has no antecedent before burial starts.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) It helps maintain the balance of gases in the atmosphere. (Q) Photosynthesis is the process by which plants manufacture their own food. (R) Oxygen released during photosynthesis is essential for most life on Earth. (S) Plants absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen as a byproduct of this process. Correct order:
questions.explanation: Q defines photosynthesis. S explains the gas exchange ('this process' refers back to Q). R gives the significance of the oxygen released (pronoun 'released' links to S's release). P states the atmospheric consequence — the broadest conclusion. Q-R-S-P fails: 'Oxygen released' in R has no referent unless S precedes it.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) OPEC members met in Vienna to discuss production cuts. (Q) Member nations ultimately agreed to reduce output by two million barrels per day. (R) Yet crude oil prices remained stubbornly below $40 per barrel. (S) Global supply continued to outpace demand despite the cuts. Correct order:
questions.explanation: P is the event (OPEC meeting). Q is the decision reached (production cut). R shows the surprise outcome ('Yet' signals contrast with Q). S explains why prices didn't recover — the underlying demand gap. P-R-Q-S fails: R ('yet prices remained low') must follow the cut decision Q, not precede it.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) She eventually published her findings in a peer-reviewed journal. (Q) The researcher spent two years collecting water samples from 40 rivers. (R) Each sample was tested for 15 heavy metals and microplastic concentrations. (S) The data revealed alarming levels of lead and cadmium in 30 per cent of samples. Correct order:
questions.explanation: Q sets up the subject and methodology (sample collection). R describes what was done with each sample (testing). S presents the key finding from the data. P gives the outcome (publication). Q-S-R-P fails: 'the data' in S implies testing (R) has already happened.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) However, critics argue that technology firms must bear greater responsibility for the content hosted on their platforms. (Q) Social media companies have long claimed they are merely neutral conduits for user expression. (R) Algorithms that amplify outrage, they contend, are a design choice, not an accident. (S) This self-conception underpins their legal immunity in most countries. Correct order:
questions.explanation: Q presents the tech firms' self-claim. S explains the legal consequence of that claim ('this self-conception'). P introduces the counter-argument ('However'). R elaborates the counter with the algorithm point ('they contend' — referring back to critics in P). Q-P-S-R fails: 'this self-conception' in S has no referent unless Q precedes it.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) The long-term ecological damage, however, was catastrophic and took decades to reverse. (Q) In 1984, a Union Carbide plant in Bhopal released methyl isocyanate gas. (R) Thousands perished in the immediate aftermath of the leak. (S) The tragedy triggered global debates about corporate liability in developing countries. Correct order:
questions.explanation: Q is the event (Bhopal disaster). R is the immediate consequence. P pivots to the longer-term damage ('however' signals a shift in time-scale). S is the broadest, lasting consequence. Q-P-R-S is wrong: 'however' in P requires a preceding statement about immediacy (R) to contrast with.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) Therefore, even at identical prices, a consumer's real purchasing power can vary greatly between cities. (Q) The Consumer Price Index measures the average change over time in prices paid by consumers. (R) It is calculated by tracking a 'basket' of goods representative of typical expenditure. (S) Different regions, however, have different expenditure patterns, skewing the national average. Correct order:
questions.explanation: Q defines CPI. R explains the calculation method ('it' refers to CPI in Q). S introduces a limitation ('however' contrasts with R's claim of representativeness). P draws the consequential conclusion ('therefore'). Q-S-R-P fails: S's 'however' has nothing to contrast against unless R appears first.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) Moreover, the salt march became a template for civil disobedience movements globally. (Q) Gandhi selected salt as the symbol of civil resistance with deliberate strategic intent. (R) Salt was a commodity consumed by every Indian regardless of caste, creed, or region. (S) British taxation of salt thus affected the entire population, uniting disparate groups. Correct order:
questions.explanation: Q states Gandhi's strategic choice. R explains why salt (universal commodity — the reasoning behind Q). S draws the political consequence ('thus'). P provides the global impact ('moreover' signals addition beyond S). Q-S-R-P fails: 'thus' in S requires R (the universality premise) to precede it.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) This is because central banks raise interest rates to curb spending and slow price rises. (Q) Inflation and economic growth often pull monetary policy in opposing directions. (R) In contrast, high unemployment calls for low rates to stimulate borrowing and investment. (S) These competing pressures make the central bank's mandate inherently difficult to fulfil. Correct order:
questions.explanation: Q states the tension. P explains the anti-inflation side ('this is because' explains the 'opposing' in Q). R introduces the unemployment side ('in contrast' needs P to have appeared first). S draws the conclusion ('these competing pressures' refers to both P and R). Q-R-P-S fails: 'in contrast' needs a prior position to contrast against.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) Despite its idealistic founding, structural flaws — especially the P5 veto — have often paralysed decisive action. (Q) The United Nations was established in 1945 with the primary aim of preventing another world war. (R) Its six principal organs include the General Assembly, the Security Council, and the ICJ. (S) Nevertheless, it remains the only global body with universal membership and a peace mandate. Correct order:
questions.explanation: Q states the founding purpose. R describes the structure ('its' refers to the UN in Q). P critiques the structural flaws ('despite its idealistic founding' links back to Q). S is the concessive conclusion ('nevertheless' needs a preceding critique). Q-P-R-S fails: 'its' in P ('its idealistic founding') still refers to the UN, but 'structural flaws' must follow a structural description (R).
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) As a result, many languages with fewer than a thousand speakers are rapidly disappearing. (Q) Language death is accelerated when economic opportunity is tied to a single dominant tongue. (R) Children in minority communities often abandon their mother tongue to improve employment prospects. (S) With each lost language, humanity forfeits a unique lens through which a people interpreted the world. Correct order:
questions.explanation: Q states the driver (economic pull). R explains the mechanism (children abandon their tongue — a specific instance of Q). P states the result ('as a result' — languages die). S provides the philosophical conclusion ('each lost language'). Q-P-R-S fails: 'as a result' in P needs an explicit mechanism (R) to follow from.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) This resistance mechanism was first identified in staphylococcal bacteria in the 1960s. (Q) Antibiotic resistance occurs when bacteria evolve to survive exposure to drugs designed to kill them. (R) Over-prescription and agricultural overuse of antibiotics have dramatically accelerated the process. (S) The WHO now classifies antimicrobial resistance as one of the greatest threats to global health. Correct order:
questions.explanation: Q defines the phenomenon. P gives the historical origin ('this resistance mechanism' refers to Q's definition). R explains what accelerated it. S states the current global severity. Q-R-P-S fails: 'this resistance mechanism' in P needs Q first, and P (history) should logically precede R (acceleration of that historical mechanism).
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) It guarantees freedoms of speech, equality before law, and protection against discrimination. (Q) The Indian Constitution's Fundamental Rights are contained in Part III. (R) These rights are enforceable in a court of law through Article 32. (S) Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called Article 32 the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution. Correct order:
questions.explanation: Q locates the Fundamental Rights (Part III). P lists what they guarantee ('it' = Part III). R notes the remedy via Article 32 ('these rights' refers to P's list). S quotes Ambedkar on Article 32 — a natural climax. Q-R-P-S fails: 'these rights' in R lacks context before P has listed them.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) However, the correlation between high HDI and strong economic growth is far from automatic. (Q) The Human Development Index ranks countries by life expectancy, education, and per-capita income. (R) Scandinavian nations consistently top the rankings despite relatively modest GDP growth rates. (S) This suggests that social investment — not just output — drives genuine human development. Correct order:
questions.explanation: Q defines HDI. P introduces the nuance ('however' needs Q as the premise to contrast). R gives the concrete example that justifies P's claim. S draws the policy conclusion ('this suggests' ties back to R's evidence). Q-R-P-S fails: 'however' in P should introduce a contrast after a baseline, not after a specific example.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) Specifically, the urban heat island effect raises temperatures in cities by 1–3°C above their surroundings. (Q) Urbanisation profoundly alters local climates through the phenomenon of the 'urban heat island.' (R) Dark surfaces — asphalt roads and concrete buildings — absorb more solar radiation than natural land cover. (S) Green roofs and reflective pavements have therefore been proposed as mitigation strategies. Correct order:
questions.explanation: Q names the phenomenon. P quantifies it ('specifically'). R explains the mechanism that causes P's warming. S proposes solutions ('therefore' chains from R). Q-R-P-S fails: 'specifically' in P signals it elaborates the preceding sentence (Q), so P must follow Q before the mechanism (R) is explained.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) India's GST, introduced in 2017, was designed to address exactly this fragmentation. (Q) Prior to GST, each state had its own tax structure, creating a cascading 'tax on tax' at every inter-state border. (R) The cascading effect significantly raised costs for manufacturers and small traders. (S) Though GST unified the market, disputes over centre-state revenue-sharing persisted. Correct order:
questions.explanation: Q describes the pre-GST fragmentation. R explains the economic cost of that fragmentation ('the cascading effect' — pronoun points to Q). P introduces GST as the targeted solution ('this fragmentation' refers to Q and R). S provides the post-GST complication. Q-P-R-S fails: P says 'address this fragmentation,' but 'this' needs R to have expanded on the cost first.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) More recently, digital lending platforms have made credit available to millions without formal collateral. (Q) Microfinance emerged in the 1970s as a mechanism to extend small loans to low-income borrowers. (R) The Grameen Bank model, pioneered by Muhammad Yunus, demonstrated that the poor are creditworthy. (S) Despite such progress, the cost of micro-credit remains high for borrowers at the base of the pyramid. Correct order:
questions.explanation: Q introduces microfinance (historical origin). R gives the Grameen validation (continues Q's narrative). P brings in the modern evolution ('more recently' signals time progression from Q-R). S notes the remaining challenge ('despite such progress' synthesises Q-R-P). Q-P-R-S fails: 'more recently' in P is relative to the Grameen era (R), so R must precede P.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) Light travels at approximately 3 × 10⁸ m/s in a vacuum. (Q) However, in denser media such as glass or water, light slows down significantly. (R) This slowing causes the bending of light at the interface — the phenomenon called refraction. (S) The ratio of light's speed in vacuum to its speed in a medium defines that medium's refractive index. Correct order:
questions.explanation: P states the vacuum-speed baseline. Q introduces the contrast ('however') — needs P as the baseline. R explains refraction ('this slowing' refers to Q). S defines refractive index — a logical conclusion tying P and Q together. Q-P-R-S fails: 'however' in Q requires a prior statement about speed in vacuum (P).
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) During the last ice age, large volumes of water were locked in glaciers and ice sheets. (Q) Sea levels worldwide fell by as much as 120 metres compared to today. (R) Land bridges connected continents that are now separated by sea. (S) Continental shelves, now submerged, were exposed as dry land across which early humans migrated. Correct order:
questions.explanation: P is the cause (water locked in ice). Q is the direct measurable effect (sea level drop). R describes one geographical consequence of Q (land bridges). S gives a specific human-history example of R (migration routes). P-R-Q-S fails: 'land bridges' in R require the sea-level-drop information from Q as context.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) The distinction matters because a right without a remedy is meaningless in practice. (Q) Natural rights theorists hold that certain moral claims exist prior to any legal order. (R) Legal positivists, by contrast, argue that rights exist only when backed by an enforceable sovereign command. (S) The debate thus collapses into whether law makes morality or merely reflects it. Correct order:
questions.explanation: Q states the natural-rights position. R presents the positivist counter ('by contrast' needs Q first). P draws out the practical implication of the disagreement between Q and R. S delivers the philosophical conclusion ('the debate thus collapses'). Q-P-R-S fails: P's 'the distinction' refers to the Q-vs-R tension, which hasn't been fully laid out if R appears after P.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) The prisoner's dilemma formalises why rational self-interest can produce collectively irrational outcomes. (Q) Each prisoner, reasoning from private interest, defects regardless of what the other does. (R) Two suspects are held separately and offered leniency in exchange for testifying against the other. (S) The logic extends to arms races, trade tariffs, and environmental agreements — any situation where mutual restraint benefits all but individual defection pays more. Correct order:
questions.explanation: R sets up the concrete scenario. Q describes the rational calculation within that scenario ('each prisoner' refers to R). P names the abstract lesson the scenario illustrates. S generalises P to real-world domains. P-R-Q-S fails: P introduces the concept before its illustrating scenario (R) has been described — putting the label before the story.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) The concept of 'tragedy of the commons' captures this dynamic. (Q) Yet rational self-interest ensures each herder adds one more animal rather than restraining grazing. (R) A shared pasture can sustain only a fixed number of animals before degrading permanently. (S) Elinor Ostrom's Nobel-winning work showed that communities often self-govern commons through norms and sanctions. Correct order:
questions.explanation: R establishes the finite resource. Q introduces the temptation ('yet' contrasts with R's limit — needs R first). P names the abstraction ('this dynamic' refers to R+Q). S offers the resolution (Ostrom's counter-finding). R-P-Q-S fails: 'this dynamic' in P refers to the yet-to-appear tension in Q.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) This is precisely what quantum entanglement appears to violate, to Einstein's discomfort. (Q) Special relativity forbids the transfer of information faster than light between two separated events. (R) Entangled particles, once measured, appear to instantaneously affect each other regardless of distance. (S) Physicists resolve the paradox by noting that while correlations are instant, no usable information can be extracted from them alone. Correct order:
questions.explanation: Q states the relativistic constraint. R describes entanglement behaviour that appears to break Q. P names the violation ('this is precisely' — 'this' points to R's instantaneous effect). S resolves the paradox. Q-P-R-S fails: 'this is precisely what entanglement violates' in P has no referent until R has described the entanglement behaviour.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) That is why development economists now speak of 'capability deprivation' rather than income poverty. (Q) Amartya Sen's capability approach reframes poverty as the absence of freedom to lead a chosen life. (R) A high income is neither necessary nor sufficient for capabilities such as political participation or freedom from fear. (S) An affluent but illiterate person is, by this measure, still poor in the most important sense. Correct order:
questions.explanation: Q introduces Sen's framework. R decouples income from capability ('a high income is neither…' — logically tests Q's claim). S gives a concrete illustration of R ('by this measure' ties to R). P draws the policy conclusion ('that is why'). Q-S-R-P fails: 'by this measure' in S refers to R's framework, so R must precede S.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)

questions.stem: Arrange: (P) Modern portfolio theory therefore recommends holding a diversified portfolio rather than concentrating risk. (Q) In finance, 'risk' is formally measured as the variance of expected returns, not as the absolute chance of loss. (R) Two assets that are negatively correlated — one rising when the other falls — can together reduce total portfolio variance. (S) This counter-intuitive result allows investors to hold individually risky assets while achieving a safer combined position. Correct order:
questions.explanation: Q defines financial risk formally. R introduces the key mechanism (negative correlation reduces variance — builds on Q's variance definition). S labels R's finding as 'counter-intuitive.' P draws the portfolio recommendation ('therefore' ties back to S's validated counter-intuition). Q-S-R-P fails: 'this counter-intuitive result' in S has no referent before R has demonstrated the correlation effect.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Para-jumbles — sentence rearrangement (Banking Mains / SSC Tier 2)
